description:
👇👀 Read me! 👇👀

This is a bipolar slider for IllustriousXL. The purpose of this slider is to increase or decrease the subject's breast size in a controllable fashion with the LoRA input values. Higher positive LoRA input values result in larger breasts. Negative values results in smaller breasts.

What makes this slider special is that it is largely decoupled from age. Making a breast size slider is not hard, making a breast size slider that doesn't overly influence age is hard. This slider does the best that modern tools allow for decoupling age from breast size, and in my opinion it does a good job at that.

Version 1.0: Supported input values are -5 to 5

title: Schmuser Realism: Chromatic Aberration [LORA/Krea 2]
description:
Schmuser Realism: Chromatic Aberration Slider - Krea 2

Adds real lens fringing to your images.

What it does:
Real camera lenses don't focus every color on exactly the same spot. Toward the corners, the red and blue parts of an edge drift apart. Bright edges against dark areas get a red/cyan double contour, and backlit branches or hair get a purple glow. Krea 2 renders an optically perfect lens, so its photos can look a bit too clean, too "rendered".

This LoRA brings that lens character back:

  • The effect grows toward the edges, like a real lens: the center (usually your subject's face) stays sharp and clean.

  • Purple fringing on bright edges: window frames, backlit branches, neon tubes, white text on dark.

  • A very slight corner softness that goes with it.

title: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Evaluating Early Stage Research Judgment
description: Do research agents have taste, the judgment of which experiments are worth running before their outcomes are known? We give six frontier models seven recent NLP papers. Each model, working as a research agent alone or as a team, proposes minimum viable experiments (MVEs), forecasts whether each will pass a threshold it sets and ranks them. A separate executor then attempts every MVE, including those ranked last, and three model auditors judge the results. Of 415 MVEs, 194 are judged sound, valuable and new, but fewer than half of these (73) are also judged beyond the seed paper and non obvious. The agents' first choices match the auditors' most valued experiment more often than a random pick, but are not shown to improve on choosing the experiment written first. Their forecasts beat a base rate but are not measurably more accurate than those of a fresh instance of the same model given only the paper and registrations. Teams cost more without a clear overall improvement in proposal quality. The agents produce many worthwhile experiments, but the evidence that their rankings improve the choice of which to run remains limited. The evaluation harness and a dataset of all 415 MVEs, with their forecasts and audited outcomes, are available at https://github.com/ArtKanke/rTaste.
author: Art Kanke

title: Preserving Utility in Continual LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Projections
description: Unlearning concerns the task of removing the influence of a sensitive portion of the training data, such as protected, copyrighted or private text, from a model without retraining it from scratch. While unlearning requests happen continuously during a model's lifetime, the vast majority of LLM unlearning methods are ill-suited for iterated removal, yielding steep decay in forgetting and utility upon sequential unlearning. This decay stems from interference between successive updates, as each new deletion can undo earlier ones or push the model further along directions already degraded by them. To address this, we introduce Continual Orthogonal Projection (COP), a gradient-projection scheme that restricts each update to the orthogonal complement of activation subspaces cached from prior forget sets. This approach provably guarantees first-order non-interference with earlier deletions. COP stores only a low-rank basis per layer, requiring neither past gradients nor previous forget sets, and plugs into unlearning methods that update the model through gradient steps on a differentiable loss without modifying its objective. Experiments on standard LLM unlearning benchmarks (TOFU and RWKU) show that COP preserves utility across sequential requests without weakening forgetting, preventing the collapse of standard objectives and forgetting more effectively than continual-specific baselines.
author: Juan Belieni, Ana Carolina Erthal, Eliezer de Souza da Silva, Diego Mesquita

title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
description: In psychiatric practice, the clinical intake interview remains a primary diagnostic instrument, requiring the clinician to establish rapport while disentangling complex, overlapping presentations. Here, we show that multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation environments improves language model performance on structured text-based psychiatric intake, spanning history-taking, differential diagnosis, and initial management planning. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study ($N = 60$ matched scenario pairs, 120 encounters) comparing the RL-trained agent against its identically prompted base model, 32 board-certified psychiatrists role-played standardized patients while a separate panel of 15 independent, board-certified psychiatrists scored the de-identified transcripts. The trained agent outperformed the base model in 76.7% of matched scenario pairs ($p < 0.0001$), with gains on an adapted clinical-examination rubric ($d_z = 0.77$, $p < 0.0001$), patient-centered communication (82.0% vs. 65.2%, $p < 0.001$), and differential diagnosis appropriateness (68.3% vs. 33.3%, $p < 0.001$). SWEAT — Perspiration & Glistening Skin Slider

Some like it hot. Others look like they've been questioned by the police for six hours.

SWEAT is a subtle, adjustable SDXL concept slider for adding perspiration to people and scenes, from a barely perceptible glisten to unmistakably sweaty skin, damp hair, and moisture-soaked clothing.

Unlike a general wetness effect, SWEAT tends to concentrate its attention where perspiration naturally appears: the forehead, temples, face, neck, and skin near the hairline. Hair may become damp around the face while remaining relatively dry elsewhere.

Perfect for athletes, summer heat, saunas, stage performers, hard labor, nervous television presenters, film noir interrogations, and anyone whose day has gone considerably worse than expected.
